newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bahn says in talks on air cargo rail link.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bahn says in talks on air cargo rail link.

text.p: Deutsche Bahn AG (DB) said today it will unveil in October a newly-designed Cargo Sprinter train to operate air cargo rail feeder services.

Michael Adam, spokesman for DB Cargo, the railway's freight division, told Reuters in a telephone interview DB was in talks with airlines, forwarders and shippers on using the train for regular rail services for the air cargo industry.
But he declined to confirm a statement earlier on Tuesday from Swissair cargo manager Germany, Ulf Steinmann, that a daily overnight Frankfurt-Zurich service could be launched in autumn 1997.
Adam said: "There are several routes where something could be done, including Germany-Switzerland. Autumn 1997 is being planned for."
He said other international routes were potential options but declined to disclose which destinations were under consideration.
Adam said DB has ordered seven units for the Cargo Sprinter, due for delivery by spring 1997, but declined to name the manufacturers involved.
The train will have two driving trailers and three waggons with a total capacity of five full truckloads, while the other two units will be used for training and backup, he said.
This would in practice restrict operations to two or three routes, he noted.
The Cargo Sprinter will be unveiled in Frankfurt on October 9 and will then undergo up to 12 months of tests to ensure smooth operations, Adam said.
Rail feeder service operations for the air cargo industry would involve particular difficulties for DB in contrast to its usual long-distance bulk goods transport, he noted.
These included the time-critical element of air cargo, the wide number of destinations and variety of delivery times before departures, he said.
